cards.title: Cash Triage: Receivables Are Getting Moldy
cards.body: Accounts receivable is bloated. We can push collections, preserve relationships, or ignore it and pretend cash magically breeds in captivity.

choices.label: Push collections hard
choices.description: Collect the overdue AR aggressively and accept the relationship hit.
choices.feedback: Cash improves, but the commercial team is already making faces.

choices.label: Gentle follow-up
choices.description: Collect part of the balance while keeping partners calm.
choices.feedback: Less cash now, fewer broken relationships.

choices.label: Do nothing
choices.description: Leave AR alone and hope cash solves itself.
choices.feedback: Nothing says CFO like watching working capital rot in a drawer.

cards.title: Vendor Pressure: The Lights Prefer Money
cards.body: Critical vendors are asking when they get paid. We can protect operations, stretch payables, or split the difference.

choices.label: Pay critical vendors
choices.description: Use cash to reduce payables and stabilize operations.
choices.feedback: Cash goes down, but the people who keep the lights on stop sharpening knives.

choices.label: Stretch AP another week
choices.description: Preserve cash now and accept vendor pressure.
choices.feedback: Cash preserved. Vendor trust now smells like old fish.

choices.label: Partial payment
choices.description: Reduce payables enough to keep operations moving.
choices.feedback: A compromise. Nobody is happy, which means finance probably did its job.

cards.title: Concessions Deal: Upside Is Not a Plan, But It Helps
cards.body: The concessions operator wants relief. You can push for percentage rent upside, demand a fixed guarantee, or leave the contract alone.

choices.label: Negotiate percentage rent upside
choices.description: Improve the weekly concessions sales base with no immediate cash receipt.
choices.feedback: You gave away some certainty for upside. Dangerous, but not stupid.

choices.label: Demand fixed minimum guarantee
choices.description: Take cash now from the operator under a tougher deal.
choices.feedback: Cash now. Vendor grumbling also now.

choices.label: Leave contract unchanged
choices.description: Avoid the negotiation and accept the current economics.
choices.feedback: A bold commitment to mediocrity.

cards.title: Close Prep: Documentation Does Not File Itself
cards.body: Month close is coming. You can fund a documentation sprint, lean on the internal team, or skip prep and let the audit universe decide your fate.

choices.label: Fund close prep / documentation sprint
choices.description: Pay for short-term close support and lower audit pressure.
choices.feedback: You paid for boring control work. Civilization advances by inches.

choices.label: Lean on internal team only
choices.description: Save cash, but add stress and execution risk.
choices.feedback: Cheap and stressful. The official finance department motto.

choices.label: Skip prep
choices.description: Do nothing before close and accept the audit consequences.
choices.feedback: The audit gods have noticed your little clown show.

cards.title: BudgetAir Offer: Growth With a Bill Attached
cards.body: BudgetAir will add route activity if the airport funds an incentive package. The growth story is tempting. The cash burn is not imaginary.

choices.label: Offer aggressive incentive
choices.description: Buy the growth story with a large cash incentive.
choices.feedback: Traffic improves, cash takes a body shot, and the board gets to pretend growth is free.

choices.label: Measured incentive with clawback
choices.description: Fund growth, but keep the package more defensible.

ledger_tx.memo: Measured BudgetAir route incentive with clawback

choices.feedback: Less flashy, more defensible. The finance version of eating vegetables.

choices.label: Reject incentive
choices.description: Protect cash and accept the weaker growth story.
choices.feedback: No cash burn. No growth story. The board will call this discipline right up until they call it cowardice.

cards.title: Route Economics: Accounting Wants a Spine
cards.body: The Controller asks how to track the incentive and explain whether the route economics actually work.

choices.label: Track incentive as memo only
choices.description: Keep a narrative note and avoid building a real tracking view.
choices.feedback: A memo is not accounting. That noise you hear is audit sharpening a pencil.

choices.label: Create separate tracking / cost center
choices.description: Pay for clean tracking so the route economics can be explained.
choices.feedback: You paid for tracking. Boring, traceable, and annoyingly correct.

choices.label: Bundle incentive into general marketing
choices.description: Push more spending through the incentive bucket and blur the story.
choices.feedback: Close enough for PowerPoint, not quite enough for the ledger.

cards.title: Service Capacity: Growth Hits the Floor
cards.body: More traffic is stressing airport service levels. The route story looks better if passengers can actually move through the terminal.

choices.label: Add temporary staffing
choices.description: Spend cash to keep service from buckling under added traffic.

ledger_tx.memo: Temporary staffing for added route activity

choices.feedback: You spent cash to keep the machine from coughing bolts.

choices.label: Do nothing and absorb pressure
choices.description: Keep cash untouched and hope queues stay tolerable.
choices.feedback: Bold choice. Nothing says leadership like hoping queues solve themselves.

choices.label: Cut non-critical maintenance timing
choices.description: Preserve cash by pushing some non-critical work later.
choices.feedback: Cash preserved. Risk moved out of sight, not out of the building.

cards.title: Board Prep: Was the Incentive Worth It?
cards.body: The board wants to know whether the route incentive created value or just purchased a better passenger chart.

choices.label: Build contribution margin bridge
choices.description: Pay for a clean bridge from incentive cost to route economics.

ledger_tx.memo: Contribution margin bridge for route incentive review

choices.feedback: The board gets a bridge instead of a fog machine.

choices.label: Lead with passenger growth
choices.description: Tell the growth story first and leave margin detail in the appendix.
choices.feedback: Traffic is up. Whether the economics are good is hiding in the bushes.

choices.label: Avoid the topic
choices.description: Skate past the route incentive economics and hope nobody asks.
choices.feedback: Avoiding the obvious: the oldest executive tradition after blaming timing.

cards.title: BudgetAir Misses the Service Commitment
cards.body: BudgetAir missed the agreed weekly activity target. Whether this is recoverable depends on the contract protections you approved. Finance now gets to discover whether the agreement has teeth or just decorative gums.

choices.label: Enforce clawback recovery
choices.description: Invoke the clawback clause and recover part of the incentive.

requires.unavailable_feedback: You cannot enforce a real clawback because the signed contract does not give you enough teeth. Governance theater is not a recovery mechanism.

choices.feedback: Clawback recovered. Nobody enjoys enforcement, but cash enjoys being cash.

choices.label: Negotiate commercial make-good
choices.description: Push for added commercial activity instead of immediate cash recovery.
choices.feedback: You negotiated a commercial make-good. Softer than cash recovery, but better than pretending the miss never happened.

choices.label: Eat the miss
choices.description: Absorb BudgetAir's miss and move on without recovery.
choices.feedback: You absorbed the miss. The contract is now a very expensive souvenir.

cards.title: Compliance Review: The Clipboard Has Arrived
cards.body: Internal Audit wants documentation on the route incentive, contract approval, Debt Desk decision, and month-close controls. You can fund cleanup, rely on the team, or hope the audit universe has poor eyesight.

choices.label: Fund compliance cleanup
choices.description: Pay for documentation cleanup and reduce audit/control pressure.
choices.feedback: Cash goes out. Control evidence comes in. The dull machinery of civilization continues.

choices.label: Internal review only
choices.description: Use the internal team and accept execution risk.
choices.feedback: Cheap, plausible, and dependent on people who already look tired.

choices.label: Ignore audit request
choices.description: Do nothing and let the request sit.
choices.feedback: You ignored the audit request. Bold. Also stupid. A rare and durable pairing.

cards.title: Covenant Pressure: The Bank Can Count Too
cards.body: Debt, incentive spending, and softer-than-promised route performance are putting pressure on the bank narrative. The bank wants an update before it decides how nervous to become.

choices.label: Provide covenant package
choices.description: Pay for a clean bank update and supporting covenant package.
choices.feedback: You sent the bank a clean covenant package. Not glamorous, but banks prefer boring people with numbers.

choices.label: Request waiver discussion
choices.description: Open a lender discussion early and pay advisory support.
choices.feedback: You opened the waiver conversation early. Expensive, awkward, and better than waiting for the room to catch fire.

choices.label: Delay bank update
choices.description: Preserve cash and avoid the bank conversation for now.
choices.feedback: Delaying bad news is a classic executive move. It works right until arithmetic gets invited.

cards.title: Board Prep: Governance Has a Memory
cards.body: The board wants a clean Month 3 story: route performance, contract enforcement, audit posture, debt pressure, and cash. They are not asking because life is beautiful.

choices.label: Build governance bridge
choices.description: Pay for a clean board bridge from contract terms to financial consequences.
choices.feedback: You built the bridge from contract terms to financial consequences. The board gets a story with bones.

choices.label: Lead with cash only
choices.description: Focus on cash and avoid the broader control story.
choices.feedback: Cash is useful, but it is not the whole story. The board may notice the missing skeleton.

choices.label: Blame the carrier
choices.description: Point at BudgetAir instead of explaining governance and finance controls.
choices.feedback: You blamed BudgetAir. Accurate, maybe. Sufficient, no.
